title: tune-nccl-overlap-kernels-scheduling-tensor-parallel-collectives
author: Ethan Zhang
release_notes: Improves overlap of NCCL collectives with compute in tensor-parallel runtime; introduces stream prioritization, kernel scheduling changes, and KV-cache sharding improvements for multi-GPU workloads. Expect 10-25% throughput gains and lower p95 latency on common LLM workloads.
description: Context: Large tensor-parallel workloads were experiencing suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and GPU compute, causing higher p50/p95 latency and reduced throughput when scaling to 8+ GPUs. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes across the runtime to improve overlap and reduce synchronization points: 1) explicit NCCL stream prioritization and reordered collective submission to favor compute streams; 2) lightweight kernel scheduling heuristics to avoid launching blocking kernels on the high-priority stream; 3) CUDA event fence placement and non-blocking sync points to allow KV-cache population and attention kernels to progress while collectives are in flight; 4) sharded KV-cache write path to reduce serialization during continuous batching; 5) conservative fallbacks for older NCCL/drivers detected at startup. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + microbenchmarks (ENG-2345) - [x] Implement stream priority changes and scheduling heuristics - [x] Add KV-cache sharded write path and lock-free enqueue path - [x] Add unit/integration tests for TP correctness - [x] Benchmarks showing perf regressions mitigated and throughput gains - [x] Docs note for runtime config knobs (per-replica stream-policy) High-level commits: see commits list. Testing summary: unit tests and TP integration tests passed on CI for CUDA 11.8/12.1 matrices; perf benches run on an internal 8xA100 cluster show 12-25% throughput improvement on decoder-only 8K context cases and 18% p95 latency reduction on shard-heavy workloads. We also observed a 20% reduction in per-token cost in our internal cost model for a representative customer workload. Related: overlaps with recent nccl tuning PRs (pr-30411, pr-29012) and the perf lab notebooks. Rollout plan: feature-gate on startup (REDWOOD_TP_OVERLAP=auto|on|off), enable by default for clusters with NCCL>=2.14 and driver>=535; gradual rollout to Dedicated clusters, monitor per-route latency and dropped tokens. Notes: added conservative runtime detection for driver/NCCL combinations that exhibited regressions; in those cases the runtime falls back to previous ordering to preserve correctness.

review_comments: Priya Narang: Can you explain the heuristic used to decide when to push a collective onto the low-priority stream vs keep on the compute stream? Asking because we saw cases where moving a small allreduce increased latency.

Ethan Zhang: The heuristic is size + expected compute overlap. For small collectives (<128KB) we keep on the compute stream; for larger we submit on the low-priority comm stream but insert CUDA events to allow short compute kernels to proceed. Added comment and unit test to validate small collective behavior.
Alex Kim: Please add a fallback when the driver reports no stream priorities (older drivers). Also add an e2e regression test on a 4-GPU job to ensure correctness is identical.
Ethan Zhang: Added runtime detection and fallback to original ordering; added 4-GPU e2e test that runs in CI integration matrix.
Jordan Lee: Looks good overall, left a couple of nits on doc wording and a suggestion to expose the stream-policy knob via the console for Dedicated customers.
Ethan Zhang: Addressed nits and added an opt-in console flag in the deployment template; updated docs. Marking as ready for merge.
